summary: This informational document gives a service provider's perspective on Software-Defined Networking (SDN), trying to clarify what SDN covers. It discusses requirements, issues, and other considerations.

eli5.summary: Everyone used a buzzword to mean different things. This is a network company explaining what it thinks the word should cover and what it needs.

subtitle: A service provider's perspective on network programmability and automation

tldr.problem: Network services have become complex to design and operate, with slow manual provisioning and poor coordination between management tools. Service providers need to adapt quickly to customer requirements and emerging technologies.
tldr.mechanism: SDN techniques enable dynamic resource allocation, automated service delivery, and programmable network control through a policy decision point (PDP) that coordinates network devices based on service requirements and network status.
tldr.outcome: While SDN offers flexibility and automation potential, it requires careful design to avoid complexity, performance degradation, and operational risks. Gradual deployment alongside legacy systems is more practical than network-wide replacement.

facts.label: SDN definition
facts.value: Techniques for deterministic, dynamic, and scalable service delivery

facts.label: Functional metadomains
facts.value: Four: discovery, negotiation, resource allocation, feedback

today: RFC 7149 is an Informational document providing guidance for service providers considering SDN deployment. It emphasizes that SDN is not a revolutionary replacement of networking but an evolution of policy-based management techniques that must be carefully integrated with existing infrastructure.

sections.title: The Case for Network Programmability
sections.content:
Modern networks deliver diverse services including IP VPNs, Quality of Service policies, security filters, and fault detection across complex, multi-technology environments. These services are typically deployed using static, manual configuration procedures that are error-prone, slow to update, and difficult to coordinate. As service requirements change rapidly in response to customer needs and market opportunities, the traditional approach of five-year network planning cycles and manual configuration becomes a significant bottleneck.

Network complexity is further increased by the wide variety of protocols, tools, and technologies in use, combined with recent convergence trends like ATAWAD (Any Time, Any Where, Any Device) that require seamless service delivery across heterogeneous access technologies. Service providers lack coordinated mechanisms for event aggregation, correlation, and processing across their management tools, leading to operational inefficiency and potential service quality degradation.
sections.eli5: Networks do a lot of different things, and each piece has to be set up by hand. When customers want something new, it takes forever. SDN tries to make the network smarter so you can change it easily.

sections.title: What SDN Means and Why
sections.content:
The SDN definition in this RFC focuses on techniques for automated service delivery: the ability to facilitate design, delivery, and operation of network services in a deterministic, dynamic, and scalable manner. Determinism means complete mastery of the service delivery chain so that delivered services comply with negotiated contracts. This requires control over how services are structured, where traffic is forwarded, and optimization of resource usage.

SDN techniques are organized into four functional metadomains: dynamic topology and capability discovery, service negotiation and exposure, service-driven resource allocation and policy enforcement, and dynamic feedback mechanisms to verify policy compliance. The separation of control and data planes, while often cited as a core SDN feature, is not novel; most routers have separated these functions for decades. The real innovation is a logically centralized control plane that can optimize route computation and enforce policies network-wide.

Flexibility matters, but SDN flexibility extends beyond plane separation. It includes the ability to dynamically adapt to customer requests, predict network behavior under different scenarios, and deploy advanced network emulation engines. However, flexibility itself must be precisely defined in light of network evolution capabilities and the complexity introduced by SDN integration.
sections.eli5: SDN is about having a single smart system that makes decisions for the whole network, instead of programming each box individually. It lets you change how the network works without touching all the equipment.

sections.title: Practical Design and Reality Checks
sections.content:
SDN approaches must be holistic and network-wide, not device-by-device configuration. They require a clear understanding of the overall ecosystem to manage hidden complexity and avoid negative side effects on network operation. A critical design principle is that SDN techniques remain limited by hardware and software capabilities. Complete flexibility is impossible because devices have inherent technical limitations, and fully modular, centralized designs can raise scalability issues.

Current SDN approaches should acknowledge past work: policy-based management frameworks, Path Computation Elements, Network Management Systems, and network programmability research have explored similar concepts for years. SDN is partially a rebranding of proven techniques, not entirely novel innovation.

OpenFlow is one possible protocol for control plane communication, but many alternatives exist (NETCONF, PCEP, COPS-PR). There is no 1:1 relationship between OpenFlow and SDN. SDN-enabled devices must coexist with legacy systems; single network-wide deployments are unrealistic. Instead, multiple instantiations of SDN techniques will be progressively deployed and adapted to various network segments. Vendor-specific components will persist due to competitive pressures.
sections.eli5: You can't make the network perfect with SDN. Real equipment has limits, and you have to deal with old systems too. So you deploy SDN gradually in parts of the network, not all at once.

sections.title: Building, Operating, and Managing SDN
sections.content:
Bootstrapping an SDN requires dynamic discovery of network device capabilities and topology so that the Policy Decision Point (PDP) can intelligently provision services. This discovery must work in IGP/BGP-based networks or in environments without these protocols, though a bootstrap protocol may be required in the latter case. Network operationality assumes resilience and high-availability features built into the design.

Operating an SDN raises operational and management challenges: How do SDN service and network management interact? What OAM tools should monitor the SDN infrastructure itself? How is performance optimized when external entities control device modules? How do testing methodologies change with customized module activation? Most critically, the intelligence resides in the PDP, which must process traffic forecasts, service parameters, and resource status to make appropriate decisions. Designing scalable, reliable PDP systems with inter-PDP communication for global coordination remains a major research area.

The fundamental trade-off is that simplicity and adaptability require underlying complexity. Automation is key to simplicity but demands careful abstraction layers between business actors, clear interfaces between system layers, vendor-independent configuration procedures, and tools to aid manageability and orchestrate resources.
sections.eli5: Before you can use SDN, the central controller needs to learn what equipment you have and what it can do. Then the controller has to be smart enough to make good decisions, and networks have to be able to fix themselves if something breaks.

sections.title: Security, Risk, and Governance
sections.content:
Security is essential because it conditions the robustness of interactions between network components. Service providers must assess the reliability of software modules in SDN nodes, including behavior under stress conditions, vulnerability detection, and procedures for software upgrades. PDP-PEP interactions must ensure mutual authentication, authorization, confidentiality, and integrity of information exchanged during discovery and operation. Inter-PDP communication within and across domains must also be properly secured.

Risk assessment includes evaluating dependency on controller technology rather than device technology, potential interoperability issues that freeze architectures, and the risk that SDN solutions may incompatibly obsolete existing technologies due to hardware or software limitations. From an economic standpoint, the impact on Capital Expenditure and Operational Expenditure budgets must be evaluated. Service providers must establish procedures during both initial deployment and ongoing operation to handle software upgrades reliably.
sections.eli5: If the central controller breaks, the network breaks, so you need strong security. You also need to make sure the central controller doesn't have bugs that mess up the whole network.
